title: NIST: standard atomic weight of Argon (Ar, Z=18) is 39.948(1)
summary: NIST prints the standard atomic weight field of Argon (Ar, Z=18) as 39.948(1), with the isotope rows in the same file.
body: PubChem's periodic-table row names atomic number 18, symbol Ar, as Argon. The NIST compositions file prints the standard atomic weight of Argon as 39.948(1). The parenthesis is the uncertainty NIST prints on the last digits of that standard atomic weight. It is an evaluated standard, not one laboratory weighing of one sample. Geological materials are known in which the element has an isotopic composition outside the limits for normal material. The difference between the atomic weight of the element in such materials and that given in the table may exceed the stated uncertainty. Range in isotopic composition of normal terrestrial material prevents a more precise standard atomic weight being given; the tabulated atomic-weight value and uncertainty should be applicable to normal materials. Isotope rows in the same file: Ar-36 relative atomic mass 35.967545105(28), isotopic composition 0.003336(21); Ar-38 relative atomic mass 37.96273211(21), isotopic composition 0.000629(7); Ar-40 relative atomic mass 39.9623831237(24), isotopic composition 0.996035(25). A relative atomic mass is scaled to carbon-12. An isotopic composition, when the field is not blank, is a representative mole fraction, not a new assay made for this card. The symbols for an interval, a parenthesis, a bracket, and a # mark are defined on world.chemistry.nist-atomic-weight-notation. This standard atomic weight is not the Chemistry WebBook molecular-weight field, which is a different catalog entry when one exists.
